messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: 3 nodes in infer-pool-eu-west transitioned to NotReady within 90s (cluster: infer-prod, region: eu-west-1). Affected pods: inference-runtime (gpu). See https://console.redwood.internal/incidents/2045678901
andre: picking this up — I see spikes in 5xx and increased tail latency on /v1/generate for eu-west customers. Paging on-call.
sara: I’m oncall, taking it. on-call escalation: PAGER DUTY -> paged. quick summary?
and re: nodes flapping: infer-eu-3a-07, infer-eu-3b-12, infer-eu-3c-04. kubelet restarted on all three. Pod restarts + containerd churn. Root cause unknown. I started a provisional routing rule to shift 30% traffic off eu-west to us-west.
ops_bot: Current on-call: @sara. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/kube-node-notready
sara: ack. commands I’m running:
```
kubectl get nodes -l pool=infer-eu -o wide
kubectl describe node infer-eu-3a-07
journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 -o cat
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep infer-eu-3a-07
```
carla: I’m SSHing into infer-eu-3a-07 now, attaching to console.
carla: seeing repeated logs in /var/log/kern.log: "NVRM: GPU HZ timeout" followed by containerd OOM and kubelet restart. also dmesg shows "kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 12345 (python)" on one node.
mike: could be driver + memory leak in runtime. which runtime image? latest 2026-02-18 gpu runtime? andre: yes, inference-runtime:v2026-02-18-gpu. We did a rolling image update last week.
sara: temporary mitigation: cordon nodes to stop scheduling, drain them to other pools (fallback) and scale fallback pool. plan:
- cordon infer-eu-3{a,b,c}
- drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- scale up infer-fallback-eu by +3 replicas (autoscaler override)
- change routing policy in console to divert 80% traffic off eu-west until nodes stable
- open infra ticket for node replacement + AMI rollback/patch
carla: running:
```
kubectl cordon infer-eu-3a-07
kubectl drain infer-eu-3a-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
carla: drain succeeded for node a, pods rescheduled to infer-fallback-eu-01 and us-west, some pods failed to start due to CUDA initialization timeout.
and re: starting model fallback for heavy customers: switch hosted model mapping to quantized-7b-q4a for eu-west routes (lowers GPU memory usage). Doing this via Console rollouts -> model-variant mapping.
sara: good. mike, can you check GPU driver version and if there are known regressions with kernel 6.5? Also collect /var/crash logs.
mike: on it. SSH'd node, nvidia-smi intermittently times out. driver: 535.86.07. I see stack traces from nvidia module in dmesg. Suspect driver regression combined with newer kernel preempt. I'm going to restart kubelet once after safe drain to see if it remains stable.
carla: node b and c still flapping during drain attempts. kernel logs show "kworker: fatal signal" then kubelet OOM. copying logs to GCS: gs://redwood-incident-logs/2045678901/
incident-bot: Incident created: #INC-2045678901. Severity: P1 (customer-facing 500s). Triggers: node flaps, model failovers, elevated error rates.
sara: calling infra on-call @mike-infra (ping). Also @ops_team we need capacity in eu-west dedicated pool for fallback—can you lift reservation limits for next 2 hours?
and re: ops team acknowledged, increasing dedicated pool allocation now.
ops_bot: Dedicated capacity scaled +2 gpus in eu-west (change id ded-3245). Estimated time to available: ~5m.
carla: after cordon+drain, one node came back NotReady after kubelet restart. I tried "systemctl restart kubelet" — kubelet fails with segfault in /usr/bin/kubelet (gdb stack: runit). restarting containerd temporarily stabilizes but node flaps again under load.
sara: we need a short-term traffic steering: Console routing -> create route rule to send eu-west hosted api -> model-variant: quant-7b and route weight 0.1 to eu-west, 0.9 to us-west for 30m. Andre, make that change.
and re: done. rolling out now. alerting SRE: increased error budget burn for customers A, B, C (top customers by traffic). Sending customer-impact note to CS to prep comms.
mike: infra found kernel oops referencing nvidia module after memory reclaim. I’m provisioning a node with kernel 6.4 + driver 535.86.07 pinned, will provision image and do a canary replacement of one node to validate.
carla: can we drain a node and boot from patched AMI? If canary stable, we can roll.
sara: yes. schedule: canary node -> replace infer-eu-3a-07 with patched AMI, monitor 15m, then roll others. If canary fails, rollback to previous AMI.
and re: monitoring dashboards: 5xx rate dropped by 45% after routing change and model fallback, tail latency p99 for eu-west reduced from 1.2s to 0.45s. Good sign.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident escalation updated to "On-call infra team engaged". Added timeline note.
mike: canary node booted with patched AMI, joined cluster healthy. Running load test against it: CUDA init ok, containers stable for 12m.
carla: starting rolling replace: cordon + drain old nodes, replace with patched AMI via ASG lifecycle.
sara: keep routing rule in place until 2 nodes replaced and stable. ops team: confirm autoscaler revert when done.
ops_bot: autoscaler override removed after replacements. change id ded-3251.
and re: final check: all infer-pool-eu nodes stable, kubelet uptime > 30m. Error rates back to normal for most customers. Reverting model mapping to primary variants and shifting traffic back to eu-west.
carla: verifying GPU logs: no nvidia module oops after AMI swap. copying final logs to GCS and attaching to ticket INC-2045678901.
incident-bot: Incident resolved (brief summary added). Duration: 49m. Impact: elevated 5xx and latency for eu-west hosted API, partial failover to us-west and fallback model variants. Root cause: NVIDIA driver/kernel interaction triggering GPU timeouts and kubelet restarts under load; mitigated by AMI with kernel pin and driver combination, rolling replacements, and traffic rerouting.
sara: assigning postmortem to @andre and @mike. Please include timeline, mitigation steps, and action items: (1) pin known-good AMI images and add upgrade gating, (2) add pre-upgrade GPU health checks in canary, (3) add automated routing fallback in Console for node flaps, (4) add alert for repeated kubelet restarts per node.
and re: will draft postmortem and share in #postmortems, tagging incident leads.
mike: will follow up with driver vendor and kernel team; open support ticket with NVIDIA.
carla: closing run: all nodes stable. good job team. :thumbsup:
